problem_statement: Use the attached reference image only as a style reference. The new figure must explain the expanded motivation for PP-VI-ReID: (1) precise cross-modal consistent anonymization, (2) anonymous image is not a secure representation without key-controlled authorization and verifiability, and (3) key protection may collapse ReID discriminability unless utility identity features and security key features are disentangled.
existing_weakness: Coarse PPA-style anonymization suppresses appearance but can destroy body contours, fine-grained identity cues, and shared RGB/IR structure. Its effects differ between visible and infrared images, creating a Mixed Gap. Static anonymous images are not controllable, authorized, or verifiably secure. Key protection improves security but may entangle identity and key/security features, reducing ReID retrieval utility.
method_summary: Follow the reference figure style closely: portrait-oriented academic motivation figure, white background with subtle diagonal hatch, hand-drawn blue/gold borders, dashed horizontal separators, Times New Roman-like bold serif labels, red crosses and red problem labels, green checks, lock/shield/person/body-contour icons, thick arrows, and compact schematic thumbnails. Do not copy the exact content; redraw the new three-motivation story. Required content: Panel (a), blue: RGB and IR person images pass through coarse mosaic/blur/noise anonymization. Show sensitive appearance hidden with a green check, but broken contours/fine-grained cues and cross-modal inconsistency with red crosses. Put a red 'Mixed Gap' between RGB and IR anonymous features. End with target label 'Precise & Consistent Anonymization'. Panel (b), gold: show 'Anonymous image' as a static transformed sample, with red risks 'privacy leakage' and 'unauthorized use'. Then a key-controlled gate with lock/key and shield. Show unauthorized path blocked with red cross, authorized recovery path with green check, and secure representation labeled 'controllable / authorized / verifiable'. Panel (c), green or blue-gold: show key-protected feature space. Put a red tangled bundle labeled 'identity cues + key/security cues' and 'discriminability collapse'. Then split with a disentanglement module into 'utility identity feature' and 'security key feature'. Finish with 'Stable VI-ReID retrieval' and a green check. Exactly three panels, labels (a)(b)(c), no global title, no bottom caption, no duplicate panel, no generic ML downstream task, no text/document/NLP concepts.
